reason: ESET update-channel tampering: returns HTTP 404 for .signed resources and strips manifest server/link/host sections. In that admitted context, the same code schedules image hash mutation, persists through HKLM Run, terminates the competing listener owner, and replaces then launches a downloaded executable. Generic updater, registry and socket operations remain neutral outside this context.
comparison: All eight section contents are byte-identical between b814 and the manually unpacked 64de. Differences are DOS-header bytes 0x40..0x4d, trailing padding at 0x21c56 onwards, and total padding length. The code and embedded configuration are identical; no second independent payload is present in the trailer.

tools: offline byte comparison and decoder reconstruction
method.execution: Neither sample was executed. No sample-supplied endpoint or payload was fetched.
method.packed_carrier: Rizin checked entry 0x42a2d0: UPX literal/backreference decompression into UPX0, followed by import fixups and original-entry handoff. Manual UPX decompression and identical recovered sections establish the shared application body.

functions.behavior: Handles -standby-mutate, -autostart, -mutate and -no-rotate. Relocates to its expected basename within the same directory, takes a single-instance mutex, rotates at ordinary startup unless -no-rotate, registers autostart, starts the proxy thread, and creates a hidden window/message loop. A second instance posts local window message 0x8001 to retrigger update/rotation.

Opens the specified file exclusively for read/write, retries 25 times with 100 ms sleeps, seeds rand from timing and process ID, appends 4+(rand()%8) random bytes at EOF, and logs hash changed. This changes the image hash without changing section code.
Copies the running image to the temp directory as eup_rotate_<pid>.exe. Starts it with -standby-mutate <original path> <pid> using CREATE_NO_WINDOW and exits on successful handoff.

Parses original path/PID, waits up to 60 seconds on the original process, sleeps 700 ms, calls the mutation routine, and relaunches the original with -no-rotate. Cleanup at 0x4153bc removes temp standby copies.

Reads/verifies and writes HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, using value Eupdate Helper containing its quoted full path. Removes its legacy Startup shortcut. If writing requires elevation, requests ShellExecuteW runas with -autostart; no UAC bypass was found.

Runs ESET ecmd.exe /update through 0x413f30. Checks for program updates at startup and every 600000 ms (10 minutes). Rotates every 21600000 ms (6 hours); an instance retrigger schedules an earlier rotation. These are USER32 timers; the diagnostic saying cron does not mean OS cron or Task Scheduler.

Fetches http://47.108.48.69:4044/eupo/info.txt into a temp file using the raw-socket HTTP downloader at 0x416c08. Parses version: and downurl:, compares the remote version against 4.0.1, and uses a YES/NO MessageBoxW. Only IDYES (6) at 0x412c77 enters replacement. Downloads the server-supplied HTTP URL, checks only the first two MZ bytes at 0x412de1..0x412dfa, renames the current image to .old.exe, installs the downloaded image at its current path, launches it, and opens the explanatory page. No signature/hash verification was found. The downloaded replacement is a future dependency, not bytes available in these specimens.

Binds INADDR_ANY on TCP 8000. On bind failure, dynamically resolves GetExtendedTcpTable, finds a LISTEN row for the port, excludes PID <=4 and itself, opens the owner process and terminates it when STILL_ACTIVE; then retries. Accepts clients into per-client handler 0x4144fc. Refreshes upstream account selection about every 30 minutes.

Decodes the account-service hostname, path, username and password in four calls to 0x416bb0; fetches https://id.1yz.me:4046/id.html using Basic encrypt:type. Removes HTML tags, parses trial-/eav- account rows, shuffles candidates, tests them against the ESET consumer update manifest, and caches a successful username/password. This acquires remote supplied accounts; it does not read local browser or credential stores.

For byte index i: output[i] = input[i] XOR key XOR ((31*i+7) & 255). Ciphertext/keys decode to id.1yz.me, /id.html, encrypt, type. This is an indexed XOR byte transformation, not evidence of AES or a payload decryptor.

Parses the first request-line target, rejects a target ending in .signed with 404 at 0x4146c7..0x41473b, maps legacy update.ver requests to fixed ESET paths, and fetches against the ESET upstream using the selected Basic account. Other request paths also go to this upstream. No SOCKS/CONNECT tunnel, received command dispatch, or remote shell path was found. Sends HTTP status/content type and streams the upstream response to the accepted socket.

For rewritten update.ver responses, removes [SERVERS], [LINKS], [HOSTS] headings and their section contents until the next INI heading, forwarding other lines. Together with .signed rejection this changes update delivery; static code alone does not establish how a particular ESET client handles signature fallback.

The WinHttpSetOption option at 0x414b62 is 84 with value 0xA80: WINHTTP_OPTION_SECURE_PROTOCOLS allowing TLS 1.0/1.1/1.2. It is not WINHTTP_OPTION_SECURITY_FLAGS (31); therefore this call does not disable certificate verification.

changes.evidence: Existing listener imports, termination import and both attempt/success diagnostics required. No product identity veto or inferred proxy abuse. Result is process termination, so it lives under process/terminate/kill.
Native byte-copy loop with two XOR operations and indexed affine key. Multiplier, addend, stack slot and jump displacement are wildcarded; endpoints and absolute addresses are absent.
Explicit HKLM Run-set diagnostic, describing login activation rather than a generic registry operation.

retained: Generic PE import, hash-padding, XOR, credential-format and registry observations retain capability-level criticality. New hostile findings require verified update tampering. The older open-proxy rule now requires SOCKS server evidence so a fixed-upstream mirror is not mislabeled as a general-purpose proxy.
ancestor_audit: New objective gates explicitly require signature denial plus manifest section filtering. Renaming the product does not remove these matches. Atomics bind code pointers and shared buffers rather than spare logging strings. The responseTransformer field moved from HTTP response processing to config/schema; actual Telegram config.get call traits moved from schema to config/read with unchanged matchers and updated consumers.

baseline_validation.cause: An ignored testdata/does-nothing/.claude/settings.local.json local permissions file contains Read(//tmp/**), triggering notable temp-path-segment. It is not a tracked fixture.

checks.cache_observation: Earlier scans using an older cache directory missed inline results; fresh-cache scans, both normal and verbose, agree on five hostile findings. The exact cause of the older cache discrepancy was not established.

limitations: Static reverse engineering identifies code capability and control flow, not endpoint ownership or author authorization.
No sample or downloaded payload was executed, and no sample endpoint was contacted.
Live account contents and future downloaded replacements are unavailable for this review.
ESET client signature fallback behavior was not reproduced dynamically.
The five hostile findings share an admitted tampering context; generic operations alone do not receive those findings.

hostile_traits.behavior: Signature-resource denial plus manifest routing-section filtering
Scheduled executable hash mutation in the tampering proxy
HKLM Run persistence in the tampering proxy
Competing listener process termination in the tampering proxy
Downloaded image replacement and activation in the tampering proxy; update dialog requires consent

generalization.required_behavior_context: The five traits share security-update tampering admission; they are five behavior views, not five independent proofs of hostile intent.
tested_variations: XOR key, multiplier and addend changes
generalization.limits: Native mechanics cover related 32-bit x86 code patterns and changed addresses/configuration. Different compiler output, architectures or languages need equivalent mechanics traits. Ordinary self-updates, login persistence and process termination do not alone admit the five objectives.

endpoint_traits.policy: Require a URL/fetch context; selected TLD plus unusual HTTPS port is suspicious context, not proof that the TLD or owner is hostile.
endpoint_traits.offline_recovery: Inline YARA reconstructs selected TLD suffix from the file's affine XOR decoder, keys and ciphertext, and binds decoded host/port storage to HTTPS URL construction.

engine_fix.cause: UPX child analysis called scan_bytes_to_findings, which discarded inline YARA evidence, then evaluated traits without it. ELF UPX and direct native children had the same omission.
engine_fix.implementation: Engine owns one YARA-before-traits entry point. Analyzers provide data and parsed context. Missing prefetch triggers a typed scan; an existing prefetch, including empty results, is reused. Regular hits and inline evidence are preserved. All analyzer trait entry points use it; the lossy findings-only scan API was removed. PE/ELF nested unpacking uses backing files while retaining logical paths.
verified_tests: ELF UPX positive/negative with logical/backing paths
PE/ELF/thin Mach-O/universal Mach-O/AppleScript direct children positive/negative
Same five formats as ZIP members positive/negative
Existing opaque-data and legacy-source inline YARA tests
engine_fix.mach_o: Standalone Mach-O already retained inline results. Direct and archive child paths now use the same engine stage; this does not add a Mach-O UPX decoder.
engine_fix.validation_alignment: The validator now recognizes metadata/signed/script, as already required by current TAXONOMY.md.
engine_fix.rollout: Verified using rebuilt cleave and an isolated atomscan linked to the fixed local cleave. Installed binaries were not replaced.
